notes: Used 4 tool calls. The QB3 Berkeley and UCSF CAT pages both opened, and both show new core-level price data. The two CAT pages are undated. /sequencing looks current because it carries the newer 100/200-cycle kits that node/706 lists as 'Coming Nov. 2024'. node/706 is an older cached version. I did not search for a UC systemwide Illumina agreement or UCOP sourcing, so that part is untested. The 25B figure of $2,551 per lane comes from the CAT page itself. It also appeared in a search snippet. Berkeley's 25B lane ($2,600, 150PE, UC rate) is only about 2% above CAT's 300-cycle UC rate ($2,551). That fits Berkeley being a pass-through reseller with little margin, but I could not confirm it. The Berkeley page does not say why it consolidated or who the 'other partners' were.

It should show which partner Berkeley used before (likely the Vincent J. Coates Genomics Lab or another UC core) and the old lane price. 3) Search 'UC systemwide Illumina agreement', UCOP strategic sourcing, and the UC Supplier Network for a UC-wide Illumina or life-science reagent contract, which is the large-account discount vehicle. 4) Check whether UC Davis, UCSD IGM and UCLA TCGB changed 25B prices in 2026.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: UCSF CAT's UC-internal NovaSeq X lane prices have fallen sharply versus its earlier price sheet, with the 10B falling most.
items.detail: The older CAT page (node/706, around 2024) listed UC rates of $2,850 per 25B 300-cycle lane and $1,724 per 10B 300-cycle lane. The current-looking CAT /sequencing page lists $2,551 (25B 300-cycle, -10.5%) and $1,439 (10B 300-cycle, -16.5%). 10B 100-cycle fell $1,252 -> $1,105 (-11.7%). Neither page is dated, so the timing of the cuts is inferred from the 'Coming Nov. 2024' marker. $2,551 per lane on a nominal ~875 Gb 300-cycle lane is about $2.9/Gb, or lower on Berkeley's stated 25-30% yield uplift.
items.source_name: UCSF Center for Advanced Technology (CAT) rate pages
items.why_new: UCSF CAT lane prices and the roughly 10-17% drop in UC rates are not in the known core-rate list.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: Berkeley now resells all NovaSeq X lanes through a single UC core at a small markup, and its '10X only' 25B lane is about 40% below a 150PE lane.
items.detail: QB3 Berkeley (rates for work after 1 Jun 2026) lists UC prices of $2,600 (25B 150PE), $1,565 (25B '10X only'), and $1,535 (10B 150PE). Berkeley's 25B 150PE price is about 2% above CAT's $2,551 UC rate; the 10B 150PE is about 7% above $1,439 and the 25B 10X lane is about 7% above CAT's $1,465 100-cycle lane. External price is $2,990 for the 25B 150PE lane, about 15% above the UC rate, against a 33% non-UC markup at CAT. Berkeley says 'all lanes are sent to the UCSF CAT Lab', transitioned in summer 2026 from other partners. The page does not name them.
items.quote: all lanes are sent to the UCSF CAT Lab at this time
items.why_new: This is a case of one UC campus moving all its X lanes to a single UC partner, which is not in the known core-rate list.
